title: Psalms Chapter 141 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 141 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 141 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 141.

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalm 141 according to the text?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:1 begins with 'A Psalm of David,' indicating David as the author.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do when he cries unto Him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:1 says, 'LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice.'

questions.question: According to Psalm 141, how is the psalmist's prayer described before God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:2 states, 'Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense.'

questions.question: In Psalm 141, what is compared to the lifting up of the psalmist's hands?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:2 says, 'and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to set before his mouth?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:3 states, 'Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to keep?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:3 says, 'keep the door of my lips.'

questions.question: According to Psalm 141, what does the psalmist not want his heart inclined to?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:4 says, 'Incline not my heart to any evil thing.'

questions.question: With whom does the psalmist not want to practise wicked works?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:4 states, 'to practise wicked works with men that work iniquity.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalm 141:1 expresses a cry to the LORD for immediate help.
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:1 says, 'LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me,' which shows the psalmist asking for quick response.

questions.question: True or False: Psalm 141:2 compares the lifting up of the psalmist's hands to the morning sacrifice.
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:2 compares it to 'the evening sacrifice,' not the morning sacrifice.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks God to keep the door of his lips in Psalm 141.
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:3 says, 'keep the door of my lips.'

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks God to incline his heart toward wicked works.
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:4 says, 'Incline not my heart to any evil thing,' so the psalmist asks God not to incline his heart toward wickedness.

questions.question: In Psalm 141, what follows immediately after the psalmist asking God to keep the door of his lips?
options: Incline not my heart to any evil thing
Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense
LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me
When their judges are overthrown in stony places
questions.correctAnswer: Incline not my heart to any evil thing
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:4 follows Psalm 141:3, continuing with 'Incline not my heart to any evil thing.'

questions.question: According to Psalm 141, how does the psalmist describe the sweetness of his words?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:6 says, 'they shall hear my words; for they are sweet.'

questions.question: In Psalm 141, what is the psalmist's eyes directed toward?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:8 states, 'But mine eyes are unto thee, O GOD the Lord.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 141 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 141 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 141:5, how should a righteous person's reproof be received?
options: As a kindness and excellent oil that will not break the head
As a burden that must be avoided
As a mere formality with no effect
As a punishment to be feared
questions.correctAnswer: As a kindness and excellent oil that will not break the head
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:5 teaches that when the righteous smite or reprove, it is a kindness and like excellent oil which will not cause harm, emphasizing humility and openness to correction. This connects with the idea of prayer continuing in their calamities, showing faith and forgiveness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 141:6 say will happen when judges are overthrown in stony places?
options: They shall hear the psalmist's words because they are sweet
They will be forgotten and ignored
They will be strengthened and encouraged
questions.correctAnswer: They shall hear the psalmist's words because they are sweet
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states that when judges fall in difficult or harsh places, they will still hear the psalmist’s words because the words are sweet, showing that God's truth and prayer remain valuable even in adversity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 141:7 illustrate the state of the psalmist’s community or people?
options: Their bones are scattered at the grave's mouth, like wood being cut and cleaved on the earth
They are flourishing and strong like mighty trees
They are hidden and secure like treasures in the earth
They are gathered and united like a flock of sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Their bones are scattered at the grave's mouth, like wood being cut and cleaved on the earth
questions.explanation: Verse 7 uses the imagery of scattered bones and cleaving wood to depict destruction or dispersion, emphasizing suffering and mortality, which contrasts with the trust expressed in the following verse.

questions.question: What is the psalmist’s attitude toward God as expressed in Psalms 141:8?
options: His eyes are towards God, trusting Him and asking not to be left destitute
He doubts God's presence in his life
He relies on his own strength to overcome troubles
He is indifferent to God's help
questions.correctAnswer: His eyes are towards God, trusting Him and asking not to be left destitute
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows the psalmist’s focused trust and dependence on God, asking God not to abandon his soul, portraying faith and reliance on divine help despite adversity.

questions.question: What relationship between prayer and reproof is suggested by Psalms 141:5 and 141:6?
options: Prayer continues even when reproof comes, and the psalmist’s words remain sweet to those in adversity
Reproof causes the psalmist to stop praying
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer continues even when reproof comes, and the psalmist’s words remain sweet to those in adversity
questions.explanation: Verse 5 notes that prayer also continues in the calamities of the righteous who reprove the psalmist, and verse 6 shows that his words remain sweet even when judges are overthrown, indicating perseverance in faith and humility in correction.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 141:9-10, what is the psalmist’s prayer concerning the traps laid by workers of iniquity?
options: To be kept from their snares and for the wicked to fall into their own nets while he escapes
To confront and fight the workers of iniquity directly
To join the workers of iniquity to understand them
To ignore the snares and nets altogether
questions.correctAnswer: To be kept from their snares and for the wicked to fall into their own nets while he escapes
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 express a plea for protection from evil traps and a desire for justice where the wicked fall into their own schemes, demonstrating trust in God's protective justice.

questions.question: What biblical virtue is primarily taught in Psalms 141:5 about receiving correction?
options: Humility in accepting reproof as kindness
questions.correctAnswer: Humility in accepting reproof as kindness
questions.explanation: Verse 5 teaches that correction from the righteous is a kindness and should be accepted humbly, likened to excellent oil that does not harm, promoting a spirit of teachability and growth.

questions.question: How does the imagery in Psalms 141:7 emphasize the psalmist’s outlook on mortality?
options: Bones scattered at the grave's mouth likened to chopped wood show the fragility and inevitability of death
Bones gathered as a symbol of strength and unity
Bones shining like gold indicating eternal life
Bones hidden as a secret treasure
questions.correctAnswer: Bones scattered at the grave's mouth likened to chopped wood show the fragility and inevitability of death
questions.explanation: The verse uses vivid imagery of scattered bones and chopped wood to highlight mortality and human frailty, reminding believers of life’s temporary nature and the need for trust in God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 141:8, the psalmist places his trust in God and asks not to be left destitute.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 clearly states the psalmist's eyes are on God, in whom he trusts, and he pleads not to have his soul left destitute, demonstrating faith and dependence.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 141:6 indicates that the judges will ignore the psalmist’s words after they are overthrown.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states the opposite: even when judges are overthrown, they shall hear the psalmist's words because they are sweet, indicating the enduring value of righteous words.

questions.question: What does Psalms 141:3 teach about controlling speech?
options: Set a watch before the mouth and keep the door of the lips
Only speak when others speak first
questions.correctAnswer: Set a watch before the mouth and keep the door of the lips
questions.explanation: Verse 3 instructs vigilance over one’s speech, asking God to guard the mouth and lips, emphasizing self-control and integrity in communication.

questions.question: How does Psalms 141:4 describe the psalmist’s plea concerning his heart and evil deeds?
options: Incline not my heart to evil nor to eat the dainties of workers of iniquity
Allow my heart to follow any desire
Encourage my heart to join in wickedness
questions.correctAnswer: Incline not my heart to evil nor to eat the dainties of workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: Verse 4 is a prayer asking God not to let the heart be inclined to evil or join wicked men in their practices or benefits, teaching the virtue of moral purity and separation from evil.

questions.question: According to Psalms 141:2, how does the psalmist describe his prayer and lifting of hands?
options: As incense and the evening sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: As incense and the evening sacrifice
questions.explanation: Verse 2 compares prayer to sweet incense and the lifting of hands to the evening sacrifice, illustrating the worshipful and pleasing nature of prayer to God.

questions.question: What is the significance of the psalmist’s request in Psalms 141:1 to ‘make haste’ and ‘give ear’ to his cry?
options: It shows urgency and earnestness in prayer to God
It suggests impatience with God’s timing
It means the psalmist doubts God’s hearing
questions.correctAnswer: It shows urgency and earnestness in prayer to God
questions.explanation: Verse 1 expresses a heartfelt plea for God’s quick attention and listening, demonstrating dependence and earnestness in seeking divine help.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 141:10 expresses a hope that the psalmist will fall into the nets laid by the wicked.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 prays for the wicked to fall into their own nets while the psalmist escapes, showing trust in God's justice and protection.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 141 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 141.

questions.question: What does David ask the Lord to do when he cries out to Him?
questions.explanation: David asks the Lord to 'make haste unto me' in Psalms 141:1, indicating his urgent plea for divine assistance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 141, how does David want his prayer to be presented before God?
questions.explanation: David desires for his prayer to be 'set forth before thee as incense' in Psalms 141:2, which signifies a pleasing aroma to God.

questions.question: What does David request regarding his mouth in Psalms 141?
options: To be set a watch before
questions.correctAnswer: To be set a watch before
questions.explanation: David requests that the Lord 'set a watch' before his mouth in Psalms 141:3, emphasizing the importance of guarding one's words.

questions.question: What does David express a desire to avoid in Psalms 141:4?
questions.explanation: David asks the Lord to 'incline not my heart to any evil thing', indicating his desire to avoid wicked works in Psalms 141:4.

questions.question: What does David say about the righteous smiting him?
options: It is a sign of weakness
questions.explanation: In Psalms 141:5, David states that 'Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness', showing his appreciation for honest correction.

questions.question: What does David compare the scattering of bones to in Psalms 141:7?
questions.explanation: David compares the scattering of bones to 'when one cutteth and cleaveth wood upon the earth' in Psalms 141:7, illustrating a grim scenario.

questions.question: In Psalms 141:8, where does David place his trust?
questions.explanation: David states, 'But mine eyes are unto thee, O GOD the Lord: in thee is my trust' in Psalms 141:8, indicating his reliance on God.

questions.question: What does David ask God to keep him from in Psalms 141:9?
questions.explanation: David requests God to 'Keep me from the snares which they have laid for me' in Psalms 141:9, highlighting his plea for protection.

questions.question: What is the outcome David hopes for the wicked in Psalms 141:10?
options: To fall into their own nets
questions.correctAnswer: To fall into their own nets
questions.explanation: David desires that 'Let the wicked fall into their own nets' in Psalms 141:10, expressing hope for justice against the wicked.

questions.question: True or False: David believes that the righteous smiting him is an act of kindness.
questions.explanation: David expresses in Psalms 141:5 that 'Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness', affirming that he values honest correction.

questions.question: True or False: David asks God to allow him to partake in the dainties of evildoers.
questions.explanation: In Psalms 141:4, David specifically requests not to eat of their dainties, indicating his desire to avoid the temptations of the wicked.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage discusses the theme of wickedness falling into their own traps?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:27 states, 'Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein', paralleling the theme found in Psalms 141:10 about the wicked falling into their own nets.

questions.question: In which New Testament book is the concept of guarding one's speech emphasized, similar to Psalms 141:3?
questions.explanation: James 1:26 states, 'If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue', echoing the necessity of guarding one's speech as seen in Psalms 141:3.

questions.question: What Hebrew word for 'watch' in Psalms 141:3 conveys the meaning of guarding or observing?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Shamar' means to guard or observe, which is the essence of David's plea in Psalms 141:3 for God to set a watch before his mouth.

questions.question: What literary device is present in Psalms 141:5 regarding the metaphor of oil?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 141:5, the phrase 'it shall be an excellent oil' serves as a metaphor for the value of righteous correction, showcasing the literary device used.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 141 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 141 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by the psalmist's request in Psalms 141:3 to 'Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:3 reveals a plea for divine help in sanctification, specifically in guarding one's speech to avoid sinning. This reflects the doctrine of sanctification, the process by which believers are made holy.

questions.question: According to Psalms 141:4, what is the psalmist's concern about evil association, and what does this imply about the nature of sin?
options: Sin is contagious and linked with companionship
Sin is only individual and private
Sin can be ignored without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is contagious and linked with companionship
questions.explanation: In Psalms 141:4, the psalmist asks God not to incline his heart to evil or to join with workers of iniquity, indicating that sin often spreads through association and companionship.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated in the psalmist’s declaration in Psalms 141:8, 'in thee is my trust; leave not my soul destitute'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:8 shows the psalmist’s trust in God's faithfulness and providential care to not abandon his soul, highlighting God's sustaining and protective nature.

questions.question: The metaphor in Psalms 141:2 likening prayer to 'incense' and 'the evening sacrifice' chiefly teaches what about prayer in biblical theology?
options: Prayer as a pleasing, continuous act of worship
Prayer as an optional religious activity
Prayer as a mere ritual without effect
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer as a pleasing, continuous act of worship
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:2 uses the imagery of incense and evening sacrifice, symbolizing that prayer is a fragrant, ongoing act of worship pleasing to God, consistent with biblical theology of prayer.

questions.question: What does Psalms 141:5 teach about the doctrine of God's discipline and correction?
options: Discipline by the righteous is a kindness and a healing oil
Discipline is unnecessary for the godly
Discipline is primarily punitive without benefit
questions.correctAnswer: Discipline by the righteous is a kindness and a healing oil
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:5 describes correction from the righteous as kindness and excellent oil that will not break the head, illustrating the biblical doctrine that God's discipline is ultimately for healing and growth.

questions.question: How does Psalms 141:6 contribute to the biblical understanding of divine justice and the fate of unjust judges?
options: Unjust judges face overthrow and will be humbled by the psalmist’s words
The psalmist supports the unjust judges
questions.correctAnswer: Unjust judges face overthrow and will be humbled by the psalmist’s words
questions.explanation: Verse 6 depicts the overthrow of unjust judges and indicates that even in their downfall, the psalmist’s words remain sweet, affirming divine justice and the ultimate defeat of wicked authorities.

questions.question: What theological insight about human mortality and frailty is conveyed in Psalms 141:7's imagery of scattered bones at the grave’s mouth?
options: Human life is transient and vulnerable
questions.correctAnswer: Human life is transient and vulnerable
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:7 uses the stark image of bones scattered at the grave’s mouth to emphasize human mortality, frailty, and the inevitability of death, a core biblical truth.

questions.question: Combining Psalms 141:9 and Psalms 141:10, what doctrine about divine protection and judgment does the psalmist express?
options: God protects the righteous from traps and causes the wicked to fall into their own snares
God ignores human suffering and wickedness
God is indifferent to human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God protects the righteous from traps and causes the wicked to fall into their own snares
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 show the psalmist’s trust that God will guard him from the snares set by evildoers and allow the wicked to fall into their own traps, reflecting divine protection and just judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about prayer and perseverance can be drawn from Psalms 141:1 and Psalms 141:8?
options: Prayer is a persistent cry for God's help and trust in His sustaining presence
Prayer is only for public display
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer is a persistent cry for God's help and trust in His sustaining presence
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:1 shows the psalmist crying to God for help, and Psalms 141:8 expresses trust that God will not abandon the soul, teaching the doctrine of persevering prayer trusting in God's sustaining grace.

questions.question: How does Psalms 141:5-6, in conjunction with Psalms 141:10, illustrate the balance of divine justice and mercy in God’s dealings with sinners and the godly?
options: God disciplines the godly with kindness and brings down the wicked into their own nets
God shows mercy only to the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: God disciplines the godly with kindness and brings down the wicked into their own nets
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe discipline as kindness toward the righteous, while verse 10 shows the wicked falling into their own traps, highlighting God's balanced justice and mercy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is implicitly affirmed in Psalms 141:2 by comparing prayer to the evening sacrifice and incense?
options: God’s holiness and acceptance of worship
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and acceptance of worship
questions.explanation: By likening prayer to the evening sacrifice and incense, Psalms 141:2 underscores God's holiness and His acceptance of worship offered in faith and reverence.

questions.question: What does Psalms 141:4 teach about the sanctifying effect of divine grace concerning human desires?
options: Grace prevents the heart from inclining toward evil desires
Grace is irrelevant to human desires
questions.correctAnswer: Grace prevents the heart from inclining toward evil desires
questions.explanation: The psalmist prays in Psalms 141:4 that God would not incline his heart to evil or allow him to partake in sinful delights, indicating grace’s power to sanctify and restrain sinful desires.

questions.question: How does Psalms 141:7 reflect the biblical theme of human mortality within the larger narrative of redemption?
options: It portrays the frailty of human life that necessitates divine salvation
It denies the reality of death
It promises human immortality without God
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays the frailty of human life that necessitates divine salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:7’s imagery of scattered bones emphasizes human mortality and the need for God’s redemptive intervention, fitting into the biblical narrative of salvation from death.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 141 offers no real evidence of God's justice or intervention in human affairs. What does Psalms 141:9-10 actually teach about God's justice and protection?
options: God actively protects the righteous and causes the wicked to fall into their own traps
God is indifferent to human justice
God supports the wicked against the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God actively protects the righteous and causes the wicked to fall into their own traps
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 reveal the psalmist's confidence that God keeps him from snares and allows wickedness to ensnare the wicked themselves, affirming active divine justice and protection.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about the role of righteous correction in the believer’s life is synthesized from Psalms 141:5 and Psalms 141:1?
options: Prayer seeks God’s help and accepts correction from the righteous as kindness
Correction is unnecessary for the godly
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer seeks God’s help and accepts correction from the righteous as kindness
questions.explanation: Psalms 141:1 shows the psalmist’s cry to God for help, while verse 5 explains that correction by the righteous is a kindness, teaching that prayerful believers welcome godly discipline.
